title: VCRI Technology Asset Assessment Methodology v1

grades.meaning: Best-in-class infrastructure security posture. Documented, enforced, and attested controls across all dimensions. No critical findings. Suitable for high-trust hosting of regulated and sensitive workloads.
Solid infrastructure security posture. Documented controls across most dimensions; minor gaps in 1-2 areas with remediation paths defined. Suitable for production workloads with stated caveats.
Acceptable for limited use. Notable gaps in 2-3 dimensions; remediation roadmap required. Not suitable for regulated or high-sensitivity workloads without compensating controls.
Significant gaps across multiple dimensions. Infrastructure risk material; remediation required before sensitive use.
Material failure of infrastructure security posture. Hosting of sensitive workloads not recommended in current state.

subcriteria.title: Asset inventory and software provenance/SBOM
anchors: No inventory of hosts, workloads, or running software; what is deployed is unknown.
Inventory maintained ad-hoc in spreadsheets for some estate; no software provenance or SBOM.
An asset-inventory standard is defined but inconsistently maintained; provenance/SBOM captured for some components only.
A documented asset inventory (hosts, workloads, running software) is consistently maintained across the in-scope estate, with SBOM/provenance for in-scope software.
All of #3 plus automated, continuously reconciled discovery enforced, with SBOMs generated in the pipeline and periodically audited against the live estate.
All of #4 plus cryptographically signed SBOMs and provenance attestations (build attestations, signed artifacts) that are independently verifiable, with continuous drift reconciliation.

subcriteria.title: Configuration baseline and integrity
anchors: No configuration baseline; systems are configured individually with no known-good reference.
Some baseline notes exist ad-hoc; no enforced standard and no drift detection.
A configuration baseline is defined (e.g., CIS/STIG-derived) but inconsistently applied; drift is unmanaged.
A documented configuration baseline is consistently applied across the in-scope estate, with periodic drift review.
All of #3 plus baseline enforced as code (IaC/configuration management) and automated drift detection that is audited and remediated.
All of #4 plus continuous, attested configuration integrity (signed/immutable infrastructure, file-integrity monitoring) with independently verifiable baseline conformance.

subcriteria.title: Third-party and supply-chain component trust
anchors: Third-party images, packages, and dependencies are pulled and run with no trust controls.
Some components vetted ad-hoc by individuals; no consistent provenance or vetting standard.
A component-trust standard (trusted registries, dependency review) is defined but inconsistently enforced.
Documented trusted sources, dependency vetting, and image-provenance controls consistently applied to in-scope components.
All of #3 plus enforced trusted-registry/signature policy at admission and periodic audit of the dependency and image supply chain.
All of #4 plus enforced signature verification and provenance attestation at deploy (e.g., admission control on signed/attested artifacts), independently validated.

subcriteria.title: Dependency maintainer-health & provenance
anchors: No visibility into dependency maintainer status; packages (including those with install/build hooks) are installed unreviewed from registries.
SBOM lists versions/licenses but carries no maintainer, ownership, or orphaned-package signal.
Direct-dependency maintainer changes / orphaned status are tracked; build hooks reviewed on major updates.
Automated alerts on ownership change, maintainer turnover, or orphan-adoption across direct + transitive dependencies; install-hook/build-script scanning in CI.
All of #3 + quarantine/block on maintainer or ownership change pending review; pinned + vendored dependencies; provenance attestation (SLSA / sigstore / npm provenance) consumed where available.
All of #4 + provenance required (unattested artifacts rejected), egress-controlled CI with short-lived secrets, and independent verification (reproducible builds) with a documented coverage rate.

subcriteria.title: System and service authentication
anchors: Systems and services accept shared, default, or unauthenticated access.
Individual credentials used ad-hoc; shared accounts, default credentials, or static keys still present.
An authentication standard (individual accounts, MFA, key-based SSH) is defined but inconsistently applied across the estate.
Strong authentication (individual identities, MFA for interactive access, key-based remote access) documented and consistently enforced across in-scope systems.
All of #3 plus centralized identity (SSO/federation/directory), enforced credential policy, and audited authentication logs.
All of #4 plus phishing-resistant/passwordless authentication and independently attested identity controls, continuously monitored.

subcriteria.title: Privileged access management
anchors: Administrative access is broad and standing; root/admin is shared with no control.
Some restriction of admin access applied ad-hoc; no defined privileged-access model.
A privileged-access model (separate admin accounts, approval) is defined but inconsistently applied; standing privilege common.
Documented privileged-access management (separate admin identities, least privilege, approval workflow) consistently enforced.
All of #3 plus brokered/vaulted privileged access with session recording, periodic recertification, and audited grants/revocations.
All of #4 plus just-in-time, time-bound privilege elevation (zero standing admin) with independently attested enforcement.

subcriteria.title: Device/workload identity and attestation
anchors: Workloads and devices reach systems with shared, hard-coded, or long-lived static secrets; no machine identity.
Machine credentials managed ad-hoc; secrets sometimes embedded in code, images, or config.
A workload-identity standard (per-workload credentials, secret storage) is defined but inconsistently applied.
Per-workload/device identities with managed secrets documented and consistently applied; no hard-coded secrets in scope.
All of #3 plus automated secret rotation, short-lived credentials, and audited machine-identity usage.
All of #4 plus hardware-rooted or federated workload identity with attestation (no long-lived secrets), independently verified.

subcriteria.title: Data-in-transit and at-rest protection on systems
anchors: Data on systems and between systems is handled in cleartext; no transport or storage protection.
Encryption applied ad-hoc to some hosts/links; no standard and gaps common.
A standard for system-level encryption (disk/volume at rest, TLS between services) is defined but inconsistently applied.
Encryption of data at rest (full-disk/volume) and in transit (TLS for internal and external traffic) documented and consistently applied to in-scope systems.
All of #3 plus enforced policy (deny-unencrypted storage/transport) and periodic scanning that confirms coverage across the estate.
All of #4 plus mutual TLS between services and managed/attested key handling for system encryption, with independently validated coverage.

subcriteria.title: Telemetry/logging data minimization
anchors: Logs and telemetry capture sensitive data indiscriminately (secrets, full PII) with no minimization.
Minimization considered ad-hoc on some log sources; no standard.
A telemetry-minimization standard (redaction, field scoping) is defined but inconsistently applied; sensitive data still leaks into logs.
Documented minimization and redaction of sensitive data in logs/telemetry consistently applied across in-scope sources.
All of #3 plus automated redaction/scrubbing at collection and periodic audit that telemetry holds no unnecessary sensitive data.
All of #4 plus enforced, validated minimization across all telemetry pipelines with independent attestation of compliance.

subcriteria.title: Network segmentation and need-to-know access
anchors: Flat network; any system can reach any other with no segmentation.
Some segmentation applied ad-hoc; no defined segmentation model.
A segmentation model (zones, VLANs, security groups) is defined but inconsistently implemented; broad lateral reach remains.
Documented network segmentation with need-to-know access controls consistently applied across in-scope environments.
All of #3 plus enforced micro-segmentation/default-deny east-west policy and audited segmentation efficacy.
All of #4 plus identity-aware/zero-trust segmentation with continuous validation and independently attested isolation.

subcriteria.title: Vulnerability and patch management
anchors: Systems are not scanned for vulnerabilities or patched; exposure is unknown.
Patching and scanning happen ad-hoc and reactively; no standard or cadence.
A vulnerability-management and patching standard (cadence, severity SLAs) is defined but inconsistently applied; drift and overdue patches common.
Documented vulnerability scanning and patch management with severity-based SLAs consistently applied across the in-scope estate.
All of #3 plus automated scanning on a cadence, tracked remediation against SLAs, and audited closure rates.
All of #4 plus risk-prioritized (exploitability-aware) remediation, near-continuous scanning, and independently attested patch posture.

subcriteria.title: Endpoint and workload protection (EDR)
anchors: No endpoint or workload protection; hosts run with no anti-malware or runtime defense.
Basic antivirus deployed ad-hoc to some hosts; no consistent coverage or management.
An endpoint/workload-protection standard is defined but inconsistently deployed; coverage has material gaps.
Managed endpoint/workload protection (EDR or equivalent runtime defense) documented and consistently deployed across in-scope hosts.
All of #3 plus centrally managed EDR with enforced coverage, alerting, and audited deployment completeness.
All of #4 plus behavioral/runtime threat detection with validated detection coverage and independently attested protection.

subcriteria.title: Network security controls (firewall/IPS/egress)
anchors: No network filtering; inbound and outbound traffic is unrestricted.
Some firewall rules applied ad-hoc; no standard and broad allow rules common.
A network-control standard (default-deny ingress, egress filtering, IPS) is defined but inconsistently applied.
Documented network security controls (default-deny ingress, egress restrictions, IDS/IPS where warranted) consistently applied.
All of #3 plus enforced egress allow-listing, monitored IPS/firewall with alerting, and audited rule efficacy.
All of #4 plus adaptive, tuned network controls with continuous validation and independently attested perimeter and egress posture.

subcriteria.title: Change and configuration management
anchors: Changes are made directly and unrecorded; no change control.
Changes tracked ad-hoc for some systems; no defined change process.
A change-management process (review, approval, record) is defined but inconsistently followed; unrecorded changes common.
Documented change management (review, approval, rollback, audit trail) consistently applied to in-scope systems.
All of #3 plus changes delivered through controlled pipelines (CI/CD, peer review) with automated change records and audit.
All of #4 plus fully managed change-as-code with policy-gated, automatically verified deployments and independent attestation.

subcriteria.title: Resilience, backup and DR (RTO/RPO)
anchors: No backups or disaster-recovery capability; an outage or loss is unrecoverable.
Backups taken ad-hoc; untested, with no defined RTO/RPO or DR plan.
A backup/DR standard with target RTO/RPO is defined but inconsistently met; restores and failover rarely tested.
Documented backups and a DR plan meeting defined RTO/RPO, consistently performed, with periodic restore/failover testing.
All of #3 plus automated, monitored backups, regularly tested recovery against RTO/RPO, and immutable/offline copies against ransomware.
All of #4 plus geographically resilient, regularly exercised failover with independently verified RTO/RPO performance.

subcriteria.title: Capacity and availability monitoring
anchors: Capacity and availability are not monitored; outages are discovered by users.
Some monitoring exists ad-hoc; no defined thresholds or alerting.
A capacity/availability-monitoring standard is defined but inconsistently applied; coverage and alerting have gaps.
Documented availability and capacity monitoring with alerting consistently applied across in-scope systems.
All of #3 plus proactive capacity forecasting, tracked SLOs, and audited monitoring coverage.
All of #4 plus automated scaling/self-healing tied to validated SLOs with independently attested availability performance.

subcriteria.title: Security monitoring and SIEM coverage
anchors: Security events are not logged or monitored; there is no central visibility.
Some security logging enabled ad-hoc; logs unreviewed and not centralized.
A security-monitoring standard is defined but inconsistently applied; SIEM/log coverage has material gaps.
Security logging documented and consistently enabled across in-scope systems, centrally collected into a SIEM or equivalent.
All of #3 plus correlated detection use cases, alerting on suspicious activity, tamper-resistant logs, and audited coverage.
All of #4 plus behavioral analytics, validated detection coverage against a threat model, and independent attestation.

subcriteria.title: Incident detection and response
anchors: No capability or plan to detect or respond to a security incident.
Response is improvised; no documented plan, defined roles, or escalation path.
An incident-response plan is defined but untested and inconsistently understood; roles and escalation unclear.
Documented incident-response plan (roles, detection, containment, escalation, notification) consistently maintained.
All of #3 plus tested response (tabletop/exercise), defined detection use cases, and audited response readiness.
All of #4 plus regularly exercised response with measured detection/response times (MTTD/MTTR) and independently validated readiness.

subcriteria.title: Secure SDLC and hardening standards
anchors: Systems and software are built and deployed with no security review or hardening standard.
Hardening and security review happen ad-hoc; no defined standard.
Secure-build and hardening standards (e.g., CIS/STIG, secure-SDLC gates) are defined but inconsistently applied.
Documented secure-SDLC practices and hardening baselines consistently applied to in-scope builds and systems.
All of #3 plus enforced security gates in the pipeline (SAST/dependency/config checks), enforced hardening, and audited conformance.
All of #4 plus continuous, policy-as-code enforced secure build and hardening with independently attested conformance.
